heading: INT. STILT CLINIC - EXAM ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. STILT CLINIC - EXAM ROOM - NIGHT
A rural clinic built on pilings over a flooded delta.
One lamp, one cot, one oxygen cylinder.
Rain hammers the tin roof.
Through the slats, brown water slides past.
NURSE ADWOA FOSU-LANGLEY, 30s, kneels by the cot, a stethoscope hooked in her ears.
On the cot lies an unconscious child, eight, breathing in shallow sips.
Beside the cot, a satellite phone on speaker, its antenna angled out the window.
Doctor, he's at eighty-two percent. His lips are blue.
units.name: ADWOA

units.text: How long since the last dose?
units.name: DR. KWAN

units.text: Forty minutes.
units.name: ADWOA

units.text: Give him another.
units.name: DR. KWAN

units.text: It's the last vial.
units.name: ADWOA

units.text: Then it's the last vial.
units.name: DR. KWAN

units.text: Adwoa loads a syringe with trembling hands.
She glances at the child, then at the phone, then back at the syringe.
She finds a vein on the small wrist.
Doctor Kwan, she's not breathing deep enough.
units.name: ADWOA

units.text: Who isn't? You or the boy?
units.name: DR. KWAN

units.text: The boy. And I've got no one to hold him.
units.name: ADWOA

units.text: Then you hold him. She can't see you through a phone, so tell me what you see.
units.name: DR. KWAN

units.text: Adwoa takes the child's hand in both of hers and kneels on the wet planks.
She pushes the plunger.
Watch his chest.
units.name: DR. KWAN

units.text: It's rising.
units.name: ADWOA

units.text: Eighty-five?
units.name: DR. KWAN

units.text: Eighty-seven.
units.name: ADWOA

units.text: Adwoa sits back and rests her forehead against the cot.
Rain drums on.
